title: Impart: Integration of Memetic Operations into Multi-Level Framework for Large-k-Way Hypergraph Partitioning
evidence_span: IMPart integrates recombination and mutation operators directly into the uncoarsening phase of one multi-level hypergraph-partitioning framework rather than invoking separate partitioners; standard benchmark experiments report higher-quality large-k-way partitions and improved escape from local optima, without numeric values.
problem: Large-k-way hypergraph partitioning in VLSI and scientific computing is difficult to scale, while standalone memetic operations make high-quality search too slow.
method_or_artifact: Single multi-level framework with integrated memetic recombination and mutation during uncoarsening.
workload_or_benchmark: Standard large-k-way hypergraph partitioning benchmarks; graph sizes, k values, cut/objective metrics, runtime, and baseline identities are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Hypergraph partitioning for VLSI/scientific-computing design; processor, memory, and implementation details are unspecified.
limits: No cut-quality, balance, runtime, k range, benchmark, or baseline values are supplied.
Integrated search may trade per-instance quality against predictability and compute cost.
Official description only; partition-quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: Bringing Graphs Closer to Memory: Compiler-Driven Data Transfer Reduction in the PIM Accelerator
evidence_span: Profiling SK hynix AiMX attributes 50.07% of LLM prefill and 78.36% of decode time to CPU–AiMX communication and host reordering; the ONNX Runtime graph compiler simplifies graphs, offloads DMA-assisted layout transforms, and fuses operators, reporting 2.00–2.73x prefill and 18.50–38.29x decode speedups comparable to hand-tuned AiMX execution.
problem: Hybrid PIM systems leave CPU communication and reordering overhead dominant, limiting the benefit of near-memory execution.
method_or_artifact: Graph-level compiler for AiMX that expands PIM-kernel coverage, uses DMA-assisted tensor layout transforms, and fuses operators to reduce transfers.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM prefill and decode on SK hynix AiMX through ONNX Runtime; models, sequence lengths, batch sizes, AiMX configuration, and hand-tuned baseline are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: SK hynix AiMX PIM accelerator with CPU host, DMA, and ONNX Runtime; memory bandwidth, CPU, interconnect, and kernel coverage are unspecified.
metrics: CPU communication/reordering: 50.07% prefill and 78.36% decode time
limits: The description omits models, trace conditions, operator coverage, transfer accounting, compiler overhead, and CPU/AiMX configuration.
Large decode gains may depend on host-side baseline inefficiency and sequence length.
Official description only; hardware/compiler results require paper-level verification.

title: HDDB: Efficient In-Storage SQL Database Search Using Hyperdimensional Computing on Ferroelectric NAND Flash
evidence_span: HDDB combines hyperdimensional SQL encodings with ferroelectric NAND multi-level cells for in-storage predicate evaluation and aggregation, relying on HDC redundancy to tolerate up to 10% randomly corrupted TLC cells without explicit ECC; on TPC-DS fact tables the official description reports up to 80.6x lower latency and 12,636x lower energy than CPU/GPU SQL engines.
problem: SQL predicate scans over large fact tables require data movement, while dense FeNAND storage can have high raw bit-error rates.
method_or_artifact: HDC encoding for SQL tables and in-storage predicate/filter/aggregation operations on FeNAND MLC/TLC cells.
workload_or_benchmark: TPC-DS fact-table SQL workloads; table sizes, queries, FeNAND geometry, HDC dimensionality, and CPU/GPU baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Ferroelectric NAND multi-level storage with in-storage compute and up to 10% random cell corruption; device process, controller, sensing, and interface are unspecified.
metrics: Correct predicate/decode outcomes under up to 10% random TLC corruption
limits: The description omits query accuracy, HDC false-positive/negative behavior, device overhead, table size, and energy boundaries.
Noise tolerance may depend on redundancy, sensing, and data distributions and does not replace full ECC for all workloads.
Official description only; storage and database claims require paper-level verification.

title: XRel-Graph: Graph Learning-Driven Cross-Layer Reliability Management in Embedded Mixed-Criticality Systems
evidence_span: XRel-Graph uses machine learning to select application-specific fault-tolerance methods across abstraction layers in mixed-criticality systems, distributing mitigation to reduce hardware-layer overhead while meeting real-time and reliability requirements; the official description provides no numeric results.
problem: Layer-isolated fault mitigation in mixed-criticality embedded systems can impose excessive peak-power, energy, and timing overhead.
method_or_artifact: Graph-learning-driven design-time selection and distribution of fault-tolerance mechanisms across hardware/software layers.
workload_or_benchmark: Embedded mixed-criticality applications with real-time and reliability requirements; task sets, fault models, layer options, and objective metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Embedded heterogeneous system with multiple abstraction layers and mixed-criticality timing; processors, accelerators, power model, and fault-injection environment are unspecified.
metrics: Lower hardware-layer mitigation overhead claimed qualitatively
Real-time and reliability requirements claimed met
limits: No reliability probability, timing bound, energy/peak-power value, task set, training data, or ML validation is supplied.

title: REPAIR: Reliability Enhancement of NVM FPGAs Through Lifetime-Aware Differential Partial Reconfiguration
evidence_span: REPAIR uses lifetime-aware fixed placement, differential partial bitstreams that write only changed LUT configuration bits, and a low-overhead runtime scheduler to reduce NVM-cell write stress without changing the normal CAD flow; experiments report at least 7x longer NVFPGA operational lifetime than commercial-tool baseline partial reconfiguration.
problem: NVM FPGAs have limited write endurance and high reconfiguration latency, making frequent partial reconfiguration a lifetime bottleneck.
method_or_artifact: Lifetime-aware placement preprocessing, differential partial-bitstream generation, and runtime LUT-update scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: NVM FPGA partial-reconfiguration workloads; FPGA technology, configuration sequences, write endurance, performance overhead, and commercial-tool baseline are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: NVM-based FPGA with LUT configuration cells and partial-reconfiguration path; memory technology, CAD flow, controller, and thermal conditions are unspecified.
limits: The description omits endurance cycles, configuration traces, area/timing overhead, bitstream sizes, and baseline tool/version.
Lifetime extension depends on workload reconfiguration patterns and cell-wear model.
Official description only; reliability and CAD-flow compatibility require paper-level verification.
